tips.text: Taeguk refers to the source of everything in the Universe and the universal law in which everything continuously goes through cycles of creation and destruction.
Pumse Taeguk symbolizes the root principle of universal philosophy and is constructed by applying the truth inherent in Taeguk's yin and yang principles.
Taeguk Sajang stands for Jin of the 8 trigrams and symbolizes thunder which represents great strength and majesty.
Taeguk Sajang is an intermediate stage Pumse designed for students to really start learning the basics of Taekwondo.
Taeguk Sajang is composed of successive kicks and body twists that require the balancing of the body, which help you improve your sense of balance while moving.
We will now take a look at the Pumse of Taeguk Sajang.
Taeguk Sajang consists of five key moves, namely Sonnal Godeura Makki, Pyeon Song Geut Saewo Jireugi, Jebi Pum Anchigi, Yeopchagi, and Deung Jumeok Apchigi.
These are the five key moves of Taeguk Sajang.
We will now take a closer look at each of the key moves of Taeguk Sajang.
Sonnal Godeura Makki is a technique of defending using two hands, where the supporting hand assists when performing Sonnal Bakkan Makki.
The hand defending the torso should be placed at the solar plexus level, while the supporting hand should be placed at the elbow level of the defending arm.

The elbow of the supporting arm should be placed where it crosses the center line.
The space between the outer wrist of the supporting arm and the torso should be about one hand blade, and the elbow should be placed naturally close to the torso.
Be careful not to let the elbow rise due to the opening of the armpit of the supporting arm.
Pyeon Song Geut Saewo Jireugi is a technique to pierce an opponent's pressure points using the tip of your hand.
This has the effect of concentrating force in one place with high pressure, as the area of contact with an opponent is small.
You can prevent injuries and concentrate your force by placing the index, middle, and the ring finger together in a straight line.
